description: Figure 19 is a bar chart illustrating the average probing accuracy achieved using different MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) variations. The horizontal axis displays the different MLP configurations, each labeled with the size(s) of its hidden layer(s) enclosed in square brackets, such as [128], [256], or [128,256]. The vertical axis represents the probing accuracy, measured as a percentage, with a linear scale ranging from 0% to approximately 90%, marked with tick labels at regular intervals of 10%. Each bar corresponds to one MLP variation, and its height visually represents the average probing accuracy for that specific configuration. The bars are arranged in descending order of accuracy, with the tallest bar indicating the highest average probing accuracy, approximately 88.5%, and the shortest bar showing the lowest accuracy, approximately 75%. The chart uses distinct colors for each bar to differentiate between the various MLP configurations. There are no visual annotations or emphasis applied to any specific bar.
